nodes.label: hosted-anthropic Experiment Profile
nodes.rationale: The deliberate opposite of the default: every component hosted, and the only configuration in which citations are verified against the source text rather than asserted by the model. Exists as a quality ceiling to measure the local stack against — specifically to quantify qwen3:8b's numeric-fidelity gap. claude-opus-5 with effort low and cache_system_prompt, claude-haiku-4-5 as fast_llm, OpenAI text-embedding-3-large, chunk 1200/150, 40 candidates → top 8, max_tokens 4096.

nodes.label: 3072-Dimension Embedding Caveat
nodes.rationale: text-embedding-3-large is 3072-dimensional, exceeding pgvector's 2000-dimension HNSW limit, so the migration leaves the column unindexed and vector search falls back to an exact scan. It also needs its own database (osc_hosted3072) because vector width is fixed when the chunks table is created. This is the exact configuration that would have aborted migration before the conditional-index fix.

nodes.label: Hosted Models Lift the Prompt Budget
nodes.rationale: Hosted models are served with a large context, so the prompt budget the local 4096-token deployment is constrained to no longer applies — chunk_size rises 900→1200, overlap 120→150, candidates 30→40, top_k 5→8 and max_tokens 1500→4096. A concrete demonstration that the local tuning is a deployment constraint, not a retrieval finding.

nodes.rationale: Local without Ollama embeddings: sentence-transformers in-process plus a cross-encoder reranker. The default profile is already fully local via Ollama, so this profile exists specifically to exercise the second local embedding path and the reranker. Needs pip install -e '.[local]'.

nodes.label: BGE Asymmetric Query Prefix
nodes.rationale: bge is asymmetric: queries expect the instruction prefix 'Represent this sentence for searching relevant passages: ' while documents do not. Encoding both sides identically would degrade retrieval, so the prefix is a provider option rather than something business logic knows about.

nodes.label: 384-Dimension Database Separation
nodes.rationale: bge-small-en-v1.5 is 384-dimensional against nomic-embed-text's 768. The chunks table fixes its vector width at migration time, so this profile needs its own database (osc_local384) and a full re-index; it cannot share one with the default profile.

nodes.label: cross_encoder Reranker (ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2)
nodes.rationale: The only profile that enables reranking. It is the exercise path for the reranker seam that the default profile leaves as noop, and the configuration whose unbounded negative logits motivated moving min_score to first-stage scores.

nodes.label: Development PostgreSQL + pgvector Service
nodes.rationale: Deliberately optional: the reference development environment uses a natively installed PostgreSQL, so this file is a convenience and not a requirement. The application creates its own schema on first use, so the service only needs to exist. Has a pg_isready healthcheck and a named volume for data.

nodes.label: pgvector Image Tag Pinning Intent
nodes.rationale: The comment states the image is pinned by digest because pg16 is a moving tag and an unannounced pgvector or server upgrade underneath a populated volume is not something to discover during an incident. The actual image line is `pgvector/pgvector:pg16` — the tag, not a digest — so the stated intent and the config disagree. PROJECT_STATUS.md §8 and §14 corroborate this: the digest is explicitly listed as not pinned, deprioritised because the compose file is now a secondary path.

nodes.label: Add-on Tier Pricing
nodes.rationale: Quantity-tier prices are computed from merchant cost inputs plus margin rather than entered as literal prices, so a reseller with only a blank item cost can use one cost parameter and one margin while a branded-goods merchant can layer setup, decoration and shipping costs into the same tier ladder without manual per-tier arithmetic.

nodes.label: Per-Variant Quantity Range Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Every cart line is priced against its own variant quantity range instead of a cart-wide total, so a mixed multi-line wholesale order keeps each product on its correct tier (71 shirts on the 50-71 tier and 11 jumpers on the 6-11 tier simultaneously) without the buyer losing a bulk discount by mixing products.

nodes.label: Cart Discount
nodes.rationale: Tiering is expressed as multiple minimum-value rows with matching discount amounts rather than a scheduling or segmentation system; date scheduling and customer-tag conditions are explicitly deferred to a future release.

nodes.label: Combined Collection Quantity Discount Slabs
nodes.rationale: Quantity is summed per registered collection rather than across the whole cart, so registering several collections keeps their slabs independent; collection membership changes auto-update eligibility so merchants never re-declare rules after a merchandising change.

nodes.label: App-Created Discount Label
nodes.rationale: The label is the Shopify-side handle the app attaches discounts to; deleting it silently stops all discounts, which is why the documented recovery is to recreate the label and update rules rather than to reinstall.

nodes.label: Best Discount Tier Across Multiple Collections
nodes.rationale: When one product belongs to several registered collections the most favourable tier wins (20% from Collection A beats 10% from Collection B), so overlapping merchandising never penalises the buyer.

nodes.label: Draft Order Processing
nodes.rationale: Checkout is intercepted and a Shopify Draft Order carrying the wholesale price is created, which avoids strikethrough pricing but means the cart page necessarily still shows Shopify's regular prices — wholesale pricing only becomes visible once the Draft Order exists at checkout. Current phase supports variant-level tier pricing only.

nodes.label: 15-Minute Invoice Reuse Window
nodes.rationale: Duplicate-click protection: if cart contents are unchanged the same Draft Order is reused for 15 minutes instead of minting a new one per click, preventing a flood of orphan draft orders.
nodes.community_name: FAQ: Draft Orders and Order Tagging

nodes.label: Server-Side Wholesale Price Validation
nodes.rationale: All wholesale calculations are verified server-side because storefront-computed discounts are attacker-controllable; the customer must not be able to manipulate discount values.
nodes.community_name: FAQ: Draft Orders and Order Tagging

nodes.label: Shopify Coupon Applied After Tier Discount
nodes.rationale: Coupons apply to the already-discounted Draft Order price, not the original product price ($30 - 10% tier = $27, then -$5 coupon = $22), so tier and coupon discounts compound in a defined order rather than both taking the list price as their base.
nodes.norm_label: shopify coupon applied after tier discount

nodes.label: CSV Export and Bulk Import of Variant Rules
nodes.rationale: Export is delivered by email rather than direct download, so the email notification address must be configured first; the exported CSV doubles as the sample template for bulk editing and re-import.
nodes.norm_label: csv export and bulk import of variant rules
nodes.community_name: FAQ: Registration Form and CSV Import

nodes.label: Extra Fee
nodes.rationale: Surcharges (handling, packaging, COD, B2B service) are expressed as unlimited no-code rules with an Applies-To scope and slab conditions, and a priority/stacking setting decides whether concurrent rules stack or only one wins.
nodes.community_name: FAQ: Extra Fee and Free Gift

nodes.label: Free Gift
nodes.rationale: No coupon code is required — the gift is auto-added when the cart qualifies and shown as a discounted line so the customer can see it costs nothing; eligibility can be scoped to everyone, logged-in customers, or a specific tag.
nodes.community_name: FAQ: Extra Fee and Free Gift

nodes.label: Market-Based Offers
nodes.rationale: A market-specific offer outranks an All Markets offer for customers in that market, and two offers on the same market never stack — the better price wins. Testing is done with a test address or VPN plus guest checkout.

nodes.label: Order Limits
nodes.rationale: Limits are evaluated on the whole cart (total quantity or total amount) rather than per product, and the merchant chooses whether all conditions or any single condition triggers the limit.
nodes.community_name: FAQ: Cart Discount and Order Limits

nodes.label: Row-Level Then Order-Level Discount Ordering
nodes.rationale: Row-level discounts are computed and applied first; the order-level discount is then evaluated against the resulting final amount, so the two can stack but the order-level threshold is judged post-row-discount.
nodes.community_name: FAQ: Cart Discount and Order Limits

nodes.label: Priority of the Offers
nodes.rationale: Specificity decides: variant-level tier price beats product-level, which beats collection-level. This is why an offer can appear on only one variant — a variant rule is shadowing the product rule.
nodes.community_name: FAQ: Quick Order Form and Theme Compatibility

nodes.label: Offer List Drag-and-Drop Ordering
nodes.rationale: When a product sits in two collections with competing tier rules, precedence is the visual order of the Offer List rather than the best price — the merchant reorders by drag-and-drop to change which collection offer displays on the PDP.
nodes.community_name: FAQ: Quantity Clubbing and Tier Pricing

nodes.label: Product and Collection Page Integration
nodes.rationale: Supports the BUY NOW button and third-party payment gateways; merchants may replace the pricing grid with a single discounted price. A single offer is capped at 10 collections, beyond which a separate offer is required.
nodes.community_name: FAQ: Quick Order Form and Theme Compatibility

nodes.label: Quick Order Form
nodes.rationale: SKU entry is manual and per-row (bulk/CSV upload is not yet available); entering a variant SKU targets that exact variant, and configured tiered pricing rules surface inside the form so buyers see quantity-based pricing while ordering.
nodes.community_name: FAQ: Quick Order Form and Theme Compatibility

nodes.label: B2B Registration Form
nodes.rationale: Built in four steps (title/description, primary contact, business details, custom fields) with per-field label, hint and validation, and surfaced on the storefront by adding its link as a Shopify Main menu item.
nodes.community_name: FAQ: Registration Form and CSV Import

nodes.label: Email Notification Setup (three templates)
nodes.rationale: Three templates cover the approval workflow: request-submitted to the customer, request-received to the store owner, and approval notification when status moves pending to approved. Emails do not send at all until this is configured, which is the documented cause of 'why am I not receiving emails'.
nodes.community_name: FAQ: Registration Form and CSV Import

nodes.label: Row Level Discount
nodes.rationale: Applied before shipping and tax so tax is computed on the true discounted base. Currently all-or-nothing across the cart (no selected vs non-selected product split), and tiering requires separate offers per threshold. Discounts recalculate when the cart drops below the minimum.
nodes.community_name: FAQ: Cart Discount and Order Limits

nodes.label: Tax Display
nodes.rationale: Display-only feature: it shows inclusive and exclusive prices on the PDP pricing grid per selected country and never changes what Shopify charges at checkout. Country-specific rates override the global rate, the countries need Shopify Markets configured, and the setting is global rather than per-product.

nodes.label: Theme Compatibility
nodes.rationale: Because themes vary, the app binds to the storefront through merchant-supplied element IDs/classes (Add to Cart, Checkout button, cart and mini cart) entered in the Wholesale Price app embed, rather than assuming a fixed DOM. A missing price grid on a customised PDP is diagnosed by checking whether the cart and checkout still price correctly.

nodes.label: Custom Price Grid App Block / App Embed
nodes.rationale: Enabled as a Shopify App Embed plus a Product-information block placed below Price. Conflicting third-party pricing apps are a known cause of the wholesale table not rendering.

nodes.rationale: One mechanism applied at three scopes (collection, product, variant), each gated by customer tag, and it also applies to orders placed by staff through Shopify admin so offline/rep orders price identically to storefront orders.

nodes.rationale: Maps every app feature to real-world merchant scenarios with acceptance criteria, and deliberately records out-of-scope scenarios in section 4 so that omissions read as decisions rather than oversights. Audience: PMs, junior devs, QA, merchant support.

nodes.label: FEAT-01 Quantity Break Pricing (SCN-001, SCN-002)
nodes.rationale: Two shapes are supported because merchants ask for different things: percentage-off for volume incentives, and fixed price per unit for manufacturers who want trade customers to see a predictable price ladder. Boundary quantities, downgrade on removal and per-variant independence are the load-bearing edge cases.
nodes.community_name: FAQ: Quick Order Form and Theme Compatibility

nodes.label: FEAT-02 Customer Tag Tier Pricing (SCN-003, SCN-004)
nodes.rationale: Lets one store serve retail and multiple B2B segments from one admin panel. Unresolved-by-design points that must be documented: overlapping tag rules (most favourable applies), logout mid-session removing the discount, and tag removal taking effect within one session refresh.
nodes.norm_label: feat-02 customer tag tier pricing (scn-003, scn-004)
nodes.community_name: FAQ: Extra Fee and Free Gift

nodes.label: FEAT-03 Markets-Based Pricing (SCN-005)
nodes.rationale: Region-specific discount structures reflect local market conditions and currency; when a market has no rule the system must fall back to the global rule or no discount rather than fail.

nodes.label: FEAT-04 Cart Level Discount (SCN-006, SCN-007)
nodes.rationale: Triggered by cart value or item count to raise average order value; must appear as its own summary line, be removed automatically when the cart drops below threshold, and have defined stacking behaviour against Shopify coupon codes.
nodes.community_name: FAQ: Cart Discount and Order Limits

nodes.label: FEAT-05 Order Limits Min/Max (SCN-008, SCN-009)
nodes.rationale: Blocks checkout outside the merchant's viable order window and must state the exact shortfall ('Add $70 more'). Boundary values are inclusive, min set to $0 disables the feature, and a min > max misconfiguration must warn the merchant rather than silently block every order.
nodes.community_name: FAQ: Cart Discount and Order Limits

nodes.label: FEAT-06 B2B Registration Form (SCN-010)
nodes.rationale: Accounts sit in 'pending' until the merchant approves and applies a customer tag, which is what gates wholesale pricing. Notification failure must not lose the submission, and repeat approval must be idempotent.
nodes.community_name: FAQ: Registration Form and CSV Import

nodes.label: FEAT-07 Quick / Bulk Order Form (SCN-011)
nodes.rationale: Capped at 50 products per order. A bad row must not abort the batch: unknown or out-of-stock SKUs are flagged inline while valid rows still reach the cart, and duplicate SKUs are merged into one line.
nodes.community_name: FAQ: Quick Order Form and Theme Compatibility

nodes.label: FEAT-08 Tax Display by Country (SCN-012)
nodes.rationale: Consumers see tax-inclusive and VAT-registered businesses see tax-exclusive prices per country; when the country cannot be detected the store default must be used rather than showing nothing, and tax-exempt products render zero tax, not an error.

nodes.label: FEAT-09 Bulk CSV Import/Export (SCN-013)
nodes.rationale: Up to 200 variant-level rules per import. Invalid rows are reported by row number and reason while valid rows still import; repeated variants follow last-row-wins, and existing rules are overwritten rather than duplicated.
nodes.community_name: FAQ: Registration Form and CSV Import

nodes.label: FEAT-10 Auto Order Tagging (SCN-014)
nodes.rationale: Product metafields (brand, warehouse) drive order tags so fulfilment routing needs no manual step. Tags are applied once even when two products trigger the same tag, are not rewritten if the metafield later changes, and survive cancellation for audit.
nodes.community_name: FAQ: Draft Orders and Order Tagging

nodes.label: FEAT-11 Hide Shipping Methods (SCN-015)
nodes.rationale: Tag-gated shipping (e.g. Freight delivery for wholesale only) prevents retail misuse. Fail-safe requirement: hiding must never leave checkout with zero methods — at least one option or a clear message must remain.
nodes.community_name: FAQ: Extra Fee and Free Gift

nodes.label: FEAT-12 Personalised Email Notifications (SCN-016)
nodes.rationale: Merchant notified within 2 minutes of a registration, applicant gets a merge-field confirmation. Delivery is best-effort but capture is not: a bounced merchant address or an invalid applicant email still leaves the submission saved, and a missing merge field renders blank instead of crashing.

nodes.rationale: One row per scenario across all feature areas, cross-referencing feature sheets for deep-dive config. Deliberately structured as merchant archetype plus trigger plus expected admin behaviour plus expected storefront output plus edge cases plus acceptance criteria so QA and dev read the same row.

nodes.label: FA-01 Tiered / Volume Pricing
nodes.rationale: Percentage or fixed discount by customer tag, scoped to all products, a collection, a product or a variant. Requires a customer tag and depends on Shopify Functions / Scripts.

nodes.label: FA-02 Quantity Breaks
nodes.rationale: Min/max quantity brackets with a discount per product or variant, delivered through cart transforms / Functions. Brackets must be non-overlapping, which is enforced as a save-time validation rather than resolved at pricing time.
nodes.community_name: FAQ: Quick Order Form and Theme Compatibility

nodes.label: FA-03 Fixed Price Rules
nodes.rationale: Overrides the Shopify base price outright for a tag+variant pair (used for negotiated contract prices), served via the Storefront API. Conflict policy is 'most specific rule wins'.

nodes.label: FA-04 Cart / Amount Discount
nodes.rationale: Evaluated on the cart subtotal after line-item pricing, with an explicit stacking config; interaction with Shopify native discount codes is flagged as needing a defined policy.
nodes.community_name: FAQ: Draft Orders and Order Tagging

nodes.label: FA-05 B2B Registration Form
nodes.rationale: A workflow rather than a pricing rule: configurable fields, an approval step, and auto-tagging on approval, using the Customer API and email. Pricing only unlocks post-approval.

nodes.label: FA-06 Quick Order Form
nodes.rationale: Inherits whatever pricing rules are active rather than defining its own, so B2B prices show only for tagged customers. Capped at 50 products per order via Storefront / Cart API.

nodes.label: FA-07 Multi-Currency / Markets
nodes.rationale: Rules are authored in one base currency and Shopify Markets performs conversion, so the app never re-discounts a converted price; rounding is the known risk area and needs an explicit rounding rule.

nodes.label: FA-08 Tax Display (PDP Widget)
nodes.rationale: Display-only, zero pricing impact: renders ex-VAT and inc-VAT columns per tier row based on country, driven by the Tax API and geolocation. Regulatory driver is EU markets.

nodes.label: FA-09 CSV Bulk Import / Export
nodes.rationale: Admin tool with no customer-tag involvement; conflict resolution (overwrite/skip) is a configurable column-mapping concern and the CSV schema must be defined explicitly to keep imports reproducible.
nodes.community_name: FAQ: Registration Form and CSV Import

nodes.label: FA-10 Manual Order Support
nodes.rationale: Pricing rules resolve on draft orders created by a rep in Shopify admin (Draft Order API) so offline deals price identically to storefront ones; a rep's manual override wins but must be logged for audit.

nodes.label: Merchant Archetypes Reference (MA-01..MA-07)
nodes.rationale: Seven archetypes (manufacturer, distributor, DTC-with-wholesale, trade-only, international, large catalogue, key account) exist to force realistic scenario coverage — each names the feature areas it needs so gaps in coverage become visible.

nodes.label: Acceptance Criteria Bank (AC-01..AC-19)
nodes.rationale: Reusable binary pass/fail statements with test input, expected output and owner, referenced by ID from the Scenario Master so criteria are written once and reused rather than restated per scenario.

nodes.label: Edge Cases Register (EC-01..EC-15)
nodes.rationale: Known edge cases carry a risk level and a linked scenario so sprint planning can triage them; several entries are explicitly 'must be defined/documented' rather than 'must be fixed'.
nodes.community_name: FAQ: Quick Order Form and Theme Compatibility

nodes.label: EC-01 Customer Holds Multiple Tags With Different Discounts
nodes.rationale: High risk. A customer tagged both 'wholesale' (10%) and 'vip' (20%) needs a deterministic winner — highest discount or most specific rule — and the choice must be documented, because silently picking one is the root of merchant-reported pricing disputes.
nodes.norm_label: ec-01 customer holds multiple tags with different discounts
nodes.community_name: FAQ: Quick Order Form and Theme Compatibility

nodes.label: EC-03 Overlapping Quantity Brackets
nodes.rationale: High risk. Brackets like 10-20 = 5% and 15-25 = 10% are rejected at save time rather than resolved at pricing time — pushing the ambiguity to configuration keeps the pricing path deterministic.
nodes.community_name: FAQ: Quick Order Form and Theme Compatibility

nodes.label: EC-07 Cart Discount Plus Shopify Native Discount Code
nodes.rationale: High risk. The stacking policy must be chosen explicitly — additive, highest wins, or block the code — because leaving it emergent lets margin leak through combined discounts.
nodes.norm_label: ec-07 cart discount plus shopify native discount code
nodes.community_name: FAQ: Draft Orders and Order Tagging

nodes.label: EC-14 CSV Import Conflicts With Existing Rules
nodes.rationale: High risk. When an imported row targets a tag+SKU that already has a rule, the behaviour must be configurable (overwrite / skip / create duplicate) and documented — an undefined default silently corrupts a merchant's whole price book.

nodes.label: VectorStore Protocol
nodes.rationale: The last change removed a method rather than adding one, and that direction is worth protecting: a protocol that keeps growing becomes a base class with extra steps.

nodes.label: Protocols Rather Than Abstract Base Classes
nodes.rationale: The consequence that matters most: a test double is indistinguishable from a provider, so 'retargetable by configuration alone' is asserted by the test suite, not assumed.
nodes.norm_label: protocols rather than abstract base classes

nodes.label: Registry And Composition Root Wiring
nodes.rationale: The registry is populated as a side effect of one import at the composition root, so nothing in the call path imports every possible implementation.

nodes.label: Lazy cached_property Container Construction
nodes.rationale: ./osc ingest never constructs a chat model and therefore needs no LLM credential; the instance __dict__ is exactly the record of what was built, which gives shutdown its correctness property.

nodes.label: Container Injects Vector Width And Embedding Model Id
nodes.rationale: The store cannot know its own vector width, and the injection is what lets it refuse to compare vectors made by different models.
nodes.norm_label: container injects vector width and embedding model id

nodes.label: Never Let A Vendor Exception Escape An Adapter
nodes.rationale: Learned expensively: untranslated asyncpg exceptions surfaced as a bare OSError traceback in the CLI and bypassed the API error handler entirely.
nodes.norm_label: never let a vendor exception escape an adapter

nodes.label: ADR 0001 — Five Protocols As The Swappability Seams
nodes.rationale: Vendor agnosticism was an explicit requirement, and it is in tension with 'avoid unnecessary abstractions'. Resolving that tension is what the decision is about: the number of protocols is five because five things are swapped.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0001 — five protocols as the swappability seams

nodes.label: Rejected: Abstract Base Classes And Framework Abstractions
nodes.rationale: ABCs would force third-party objects and test doubles to inherit from OSC's hierarchy; adopting a framework's abstractions would tie the domain model to its release cadence.
nodes.norm_label: rejected: abstract base classes and framework abstractions

nodes.label: Protocols Are Enforced Only Statically
nodes.rationale: Nothing at runtime checks a registered provider satisfies ChatModel, which makes mypy --strict load-bearing architecture rather than hygiene.

nodes.label: Provider-Specific Tuning Lives In Untyped options
nodes.rationale: A typed config per provider would put provider knowledge back in the settings schema.
nodes.norm_label: provider-specific tuning lives in untyped options

nodes.label: ADR 0002 — Adopt LangChain For Undifferentiated Work Only
nodes.rationale: The Phase 1 rejection was right about the framework and wrong about the libraries: what was treated as one decision was several, and two of the smaller ones deserved a different answer.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0002 — adopt langchain for undifferentiated work only

nodes.rationale: One request produces one trace that survives the process, so a developer can see where time went hours later on a different machine. Reproducing the request does not work: generation is non-deterministic and the answer under investigation is usually the odd one out.

nodes.label: trace.py (context-var span tree)
nodes.rationale: span() outside a trace returns a detached span that records nothing, which is why instrumented code carries no `if tracing:` branches. trace() nested inside another trace extends rather than forks, so retrieve is both a whole operation and a stage of a larger one with no conditional. ContextVar storage gives concurrent asyncio tasks independent traces for free.

nodes.label: store.py (append-only JSONL trace log)
nodes.rationale: Rotation, not rewriting: appending is O(1). Writing never raises, because instrumentation that can break the thing it observes is a liability precisely because it is trusted.

nodes.label: render.py (waterfall renderer)
nodes.rationale: Bars positioned by offset and sized by duration, so 'these ran back to back' and 'this one dominated' are distinguishable at a glance rather than by reading numbers.

nodes.rationale: A traces table puts write load on the primary datastore for a debugging feature and disappears exactly when the database is what is broken; OTel is the right destination once traces leave the host but the wrong answer for a terminal; a daemon to read a trace is worse than the problem. nodes.label: The Logging System
nodes.rationale: What the system did, recorded durably — the other half of observability. Two streams under .osc/logs/, both fed through a queue with a trace-context filter and a redaction filter before any handler sees a record.

nodes.label: Logging and Tracing Answer Different Questions
nodes.rationale: A trace is a tree answering "how did this execution spend its time"; a log is a flat stream answering "what happened across all executions". A trace cannot tell you the same failure happened 40 times overnight; a log cannot show you which stage was slow. They are joined by exactly one field: trace_id.
nodes.norm_label: logging and tracing answer different questions

nodes.label: The Span Bridge
nodes.rationale: Logging does not add instrumentation; it subscribes to the instrumentation that exists. One hook in trace.py's span-exit path emits a TRACE record per stage, giving retrieve, embed_query, search, threshold, rerank, generate, finalise, load_hashes, document, chunk, embed, store and prune their log lines with no modification to any pipeline, provider, chunker or store. It costs one isEnabledFor check when unused.

nodes.label: trace_id Stamped on Every Log Record
nodes.rationale: A logging.Filter reads the tracer's context var and stamps it. Without this field, logs and traces are two piles of facts about the same request with nothing joining them; with it, any log line expands into a full waterfall via `./osc trace <id>`.
nodes.norm_label: trace_id stamped on every log record

nodes.label: Writing Is Off the Calling Thread
nodes.rationale: Every handler sits behind a QueueHandler/QueueListener pair so a log call costs an enqueue. Logging that blocks a request on fsync is logging that gets deleted the first time it appears in a latency profile. The cost is a background thread per process and records lost on a hard kill.
nodes.norm_label: writing is off the calling thread

nodes.label: Disk Bounded by Construction
nodes.rationale: max_bytes * (backup_count + 1), roughly 60 MB by default, with the oldest rotated file deleted rather than archived. The trade is that retention windows are not predictable — a quiet week keeps more history than a busy hour.

nodes.label: Redaction Filter and NEVER_REDACT
nodes.rationale: Matched on field name rather than value, because a value-inspecting heuristic both misses novel formats and mangles legitimate content. Applied on the queue entry rather than in a formatter, because a secret suppressed on disk and printed to stdout is a secret that leaked. The allowlist earned its place: input_tokens contains "token" and is a cost measurement.

nodes.label: Corpus Text Reduced to a Length
nodes.rationale: question, answer, query, text and prompt become `<47 chars>` unless capture_payloads is on — keeping every timing and count an investigation needs while keeping corpus content out of a file that tends to get shipped elsewhere. capture_payloads cannot re-enable credential redaction.
nodes.norm_label: corpus text reduced to a length

nodes.label: TRACE Level (5)
nodes.rationale: Somewhere to put per-stage detail that would be unbearable at DEBUG. Third-party libraries are pinned to WARNING regardless, because raising our level to watch our own pipeline must not turn on every vendor SDK's unstructured debug stream into a JSONL file.

nodes.label: The Console Can Be Quieter Than the File
nodes.rationale: An interactive CLI command prints its answer rather than a JSON stream, but the file keeps recording at the configured level. Quietening the terminal must not throw away the log, which is the easy mistake when one level controls both destinations — hence configure_logging's separate console_level.
nodes.norm_label: the console can be quieter than the file

nodes.label: The Audit Stream
nodes.rationale: One record per answered question, written from generation/answerer.py so both buffered and streaming paths are covered by one call site. Separate because operational logs roll off in hours under TRACE while "which passages did we show this user in March" must outlive that — one stream would mean one retention policy and the debug firehose would win. Pinned at INFO so raising the root level cannot silently stop recording.

nodes.label: The cli.command Record
nodes.rationale: Emitted by load(), which every command calls. Without it the log is a stream of identical settings.resolved and component.built records with no way to tell an ask from an ingest from a doctor, because every command initialises the same way. It reads sys.argv rather than the click context because typer invokes a callback outside the context click.get_current_context reads; the positional tail is payload and appears only under capture_payloads.

nodes.label: ./osc logs Is a Discovery Command, Not a Viewer
nodes.rationale: tail, grep and jq already read JSONL better than anything worth writing; the hard part is knowing which file to point them at once rotation has produced six.
nodes.norm_label: ./osc logs is a discovery command, not a viewer

nodes.label: ADR 0009 — Persistent Logging on the Standard Library, Fed by the Span Stream
nodes.rationale: Accepted, Phase 5. OSC had structured logging to stdout only across 30 call sites in 13 modules: no history, no correlation, no coverage, no level below DEBUG. The shaping constraint was that pipelines, providers, chunkers, the evaluation harness and the LangChain integration were out of scope for modification, so coverage had to come from somewhere other than new call sites in them.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0009 — persistent logging on the standard library, fed by the span stream

nodes.label: Everything Else Is Stdlib
nodes.rationale: structlog and loguru are good and neither earns a dependency: the formatter is 15 lines, the filters 20, and rotation and async writing come from the standard library either way. A dependency would also put a third-party API on the one code path that must keep working while everything else is broken.

nodes.label: Size-Based Rotation, Not Time-Based
nodes.rationale: TimedRotatingFileHandler gives predictable windows and no ceiling at all — one busy day can produce an arbitrarily large file. For a service that can get busy, bounded disk is the guarantee worth having. Doing both needs a custom handler subclass for a guarantee size-based already provides.

nodes.label: Rejected — Hand-Written Log Lines in Every Pipeline
nodes.rationale: The obvious way to get coverage, and it would have meant editing retrieval, ingestion, generation, chunking and the providers — all out of scope — and maintaining a second set of instrumentation that drifts from the spans on the first change nobody makes twice.
nodes.norm_label: rejected — hand-written log lines in every pipeline

nodes.label: Rejected — Replace the Trace Store With Logs
nodes.rationale: Tempting — one persistence mechanism instead of two. Rejected because a trace is a tree and a log is a stream, and reassembling a waterfall from interleaved lines across concurrent requests is work the trace store already avoids. They persist separately and are joined by trace_id.
nodes.norm_label: rejected — replace the trace store with logs

nodes.label: QueueHandler.prepare() Strips exc_info
nodes.rationale: The stdlib strips exc_info to make records picklable across a process boundary. Our queue is consumed by a thread in the same process, so the stripping bought nothing and silently deleted every traceback — the worst thing a logging system can do quietly. Fixed with a prepare() override and a regression test.

nodes.rationale: Both defects — stripped tracebacks and redacted token counts — were found by reading the output of a real run, not by construction and not by a test. The lesson recorded is that reading real output is the only way to find them.

nodes.label: Graphify
nodes.rationale: Builds a persistent knowledge graph from a repository — nodes for symbols, files and concepts, edges, community detection, and query/path/explain operations. Used so a new session navigates instead of recursively reading; it answers structural questions the code cannot (affected, god-nodes); and it acts as an outside observer on the architecture, usually right when it disagrees with the intended design.

nodes.label: A Test Double Was the Most Connected Node
nodes.rationale: An earlier build reported StubEmbeddingModel ahead of every real component — the graph's way of saying that the test suite, not production wiring, was what exercised every seam. It has since been displaced by MemoryVectorStore and Document. No architecture document would have surfaced that; it came from measuring the graph.
nodes.norm_label: a test double was the most connected node

nodes.label: Fewer Nodes, More Edges
nodes.rationale: 2086/4572 became 1981/4624 — density 2.19 to 2.33 — because 429 structural heading stubs were replaced by 324 semantic concepts carrying rationale, citations and hyperedges. When a rebuild shrinks, check the edge count before assuming loss; to_json's shrink guard exists to force exactly that check.

nodes.label: Rebuilding Needs the office and sql Extras
nodes.rationale: Without `office` the four scenario documents are reported as skipped_sensitive and silently dropped, which hid ~42% of the real corpus from the graph for two phases; without `sql`, migrations/001_init.sql contributes nothing. `graphify update` is AST-only and will not pick up changed prose in docs/, so editing documentation needs a full rebuild plus `graphify export wiki` or wiki/ silently describes the previous graph.
nodes.norm_label: rebuilding needs the office and sql extras

nodes.label: Dangling-Endpoint Edges Are Mostly Not a Defect
nodes.rationale: Of 273 in a full rebuild, 245 were imports edges pointing at third-party packages and stdlib — the graph declining to invent nodes for things outside the corpus, not losing them. Only ~17 were genuine unresolved cross-chunk references. The incremental build reports 0 because build_merge resolves against the graph it merges into rather than one chunk.
nodes.norm_label: dangling-endpoint edges are mostly not a defect

nodes.label: Ponytail
nodes.rationale: A development discipline forcing the laziest solution that actually works, on the claim that the best code is the code never written. It makes the handbook's "avoid unnecessary abstractions" operational — a checklist that runs before code is written rather than a principle invoked during review, when the code exists and deleting it feels like waste. The targeted failure mode is specific: a RAG platform invites a plugin system for retrievers, a rules engine for chunking, an abstraction over the abstraction.

nodes.label: The Ponytail Ladder
nodes.rationale: Stop at the first rung that holds: does this need to exist at all, is it already in this codebase, does the standard library do it, does a native platform feature cover it, does an installed dependency solve it, can it be one line, and only then the minimum code that works.

nodes.label: Lazy at the Core, Strict at the Edges
nodes.rationale: Input validation at trust boundaries, error handling that prevents data loss, security measures and anything explicitly requested are never simplified away — which is why settings.py, api/schemas.py and evaluation/dataset.py use full Pydantic validation while types.py uses bare frozen dataclasses. The domain types are constructed internally; the other three parse untrusted input.
nodes.norm_label: lazy at the core, strict at the edges

nodes.label: The ponytail: Comment Convention
nodes.rationale: A deliberate simplification that cuts a real corner with a known ceiling is marked in the source, naming the ceiling and the upgrade path. This is what makes the discipline safe rather than merely fast: a shortcut with a named upgrade path is a decision, an unmarked one is technical debt nobody remembers taking on. Currently one marker exists, in observability/store.py.

nodes.label: Evaluation Harness
nodes.source_location: Why this exists / How it is put together
nodes.rationale: Before it every quality claim was an opinion: chunk size, overlap, top_k, candidates, hybrid, reranking off, rewriting off were all reasoned rather than measured, so nobody could find out which were wrong and work stopped being cumulative. Four modules (dataset, metrics, judge, runner) with one dependency direction, composing the REAL Container-built pipelines — an evaluation that ran against a special code path would measure the special code path.

nodes.label: Golden Set
nodes.rationale: 86 cases, 81 with known-correct source documents and 5 the corpus genuinely cannot answer. Two curation rules matter more than the case count: questions are phrased as a user would ask, never copied from a heading (verbatim headings measure string matching and report it as retrieval quality); expected_facts are short, distinctive and load-bearing, because anything longer scores the model's phrasing rather than its correctness.

nodes.label: Document-Level Relevance Scoring
nodes.source_location: Why relevance is scored at document level, not chunk level
nodes.rationale: Chunk ids derive from chunk boundaries, so changing the chunker or its size changes every chunk id — which would invalidate the golden set on precisely the experiment it exists to run. Document identity survives that change; chunk identity does not. Document paths are also verifiable by a human curator and read sensibly in a review diff.

nodes.label: Abstention Cases in the Golden Set
nodes.source_location: Why abstention cases are in the set
nodes.rationale: Without them an evaluation rewards a model that answers everything confidently — the exact failure this system is architected against. Five unanswerable questions are five chances to catch an abstention-path regression and cost nothing to maintain.
nodes.norm_label: abstention cases in the golden set

nodes.label: Golden-Set Path Guard
nodes.source_location: The guard that stops a typo reading as a regression
nodes.rationale: A mistyped relevant_documents path and a genuine retrieval miss both score recall 0, and only one is a bug in the search stack. Checking every path against what is indexed before the run turns thirty minutes of investigation into one line naming the file.

nodes.label: recall@k
nodes.rationale: The headline metric: generation cannot recover from a passage that was never fetched, so recall bounds every downstream metric.

nodes.label: precision@k
nodes.rationale: Divides by k, not by results actually returned: returning three where five were requested is a real cost because the unfilled slots were context the model could have had. Low by construction when most cases have one relevant document.

nodes.label: Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR)
nodes.rationale: Measures ordering where recall measures presence. A correct passage ranked 8th in a top-5 retrieval is a passage the model never saw.

nodes.label: hit_rate@k
nodes.rationale: Disambiguates a recall of 0.7: every question partly answered, or seven answered and three missed entirely. Different corpora, different work.

nodes.label: citation_coverage
nodes.rationale: Catches a model answering without grounding.

nodes.label: groundedness
nodes.rationale: Catches a fabricated citation without a judge. Impossible on Anthropic's native path; on the marker-parsing path it is the exact failure mode being measured.

nodes.label: citation_precision
nodes.rationale: Catches citing something real but irrelevant.

nodes.label: fact_match
nodes.rationale: Catches the local model's numeric-fidelity gap — right passage, right citation, wrong number. It is substring matching: brittle in one direction and blind in the other, a floor on correctness rather than a measure of it.

nodes.label: abstention_accuracy
nodes.rationale: Catches hallucination on out-of-corpus questions. Computed over only six cases, so it is far noisier than fact_match over forty-seven — which is why the gate derives n per metric.

nodes.label: LLM-as-Judge Faithfulness
nodes.rationale: Opt-in because it doubles model calls and measures with an instrument made of the same material as the thing measured. Uses fast_llm rather than llm deliberately — judging a model with the identical model mostly measures self-agreement, and fast_llm is the seam an operator can point at a stronger model. An unreachable judge records None, not a default: inflating a metric or blaming the system under test for an instrument failure are both worse than an absent number. It is a biased estimator, valid only as a relative measure between runs.

nodes.label: Deterministic Metrics Gate CI
nodes.rationale: A gate that can change its mind between two runs of the same commit is not a gate. Hence retrieval-only in CI; the LLM judge is opt-in and for depth.

nodes.label: Evaluation CI Gate
nodes.rationale: No thresholds are typed. Each suite compares against its committed baseline with tolerances derived from the run it judges, and trade-off guards block an improvement bought with a regression elsewhere — which per-metric thresholds cannot see.

nodes.label: Configuration Travels With the Numbers
nodes.source_location: Three load-bearing properties / Running a comparison
nodes.rationale: A result JSON carries the chunker, retrieval settings, reranker and both model ids, and the comparison prints every configuration key that differs — the cheapest possible defence against comparing two different systems and calling it a result.

nodes.label: A Case Never Aborts the Run
nodes.rationale: A provider timeout on question 34 of 86 must not discard 33 collected results. Recorded as a failed case, excluded from every quality mean, counted separately. A fragile harness does not get run, and one that averages a timeout in as a zero teaches the team the dashboard is noise.
nodes.norm_label: a case never aborts the run

nodes.label: Every Case Records Its Trace Id
nodes.rationale: The report says recall was 0.93; the trace id on the six cases that missed says why, expandable long after the run finished. Without it a bad number is the start of a reproduction rather than an explanation.
nodes.norm_label: every case records its trace id

nodes.label: An Absent Metric Is Not a Zero Metric
nodes.source_location: A metric that is absent is not a metric that is zero
nodes.rationale: The harness's first defect: fact_match is computed as 'no expected fact was missing', so a retrieval-only run that generated nothing scored a perfect 1.0 for work it never did. Omitting the keys also makes compare refuse to diff a retrieval-only run against a full one.
nodes.norm_label: an absent metric is not a zero metric

nodes.label: --reindex After a Chunker Change
nodes.rationale: Changing the chunker invalidates every stored chunk while every content hash still matches, so an ordinary sync reports 'skipped' and silently measures the old index under the new label.

nodes.label: Request Path
nodes.rationale: Session context → rewrite → search → threshold → rerank → generate → cite, or abstain. Every stage is a timed span in one trace. Query rewriting is on by default since Phase 6 on a measurement: it is the only path by which history reaches retrieval, and with it off conversational memory's measured contribution to retrieval was exactly zero (follow_up_lift 0.000 → +0.177).

nodes.label: Ingestion Path
nodes.rationale: Idempotent and incremental: unchanged documents skipped by content hash, changed documents replaced atomically, absent documents pruned. A file present but unreadable today is recorded as a failure and exempted from pruning — the distinction between 'deleted at source' and 'temporarily unparseable' is the difference between a correct sync and permanent data loss.

nodes.label: Abstention Is a Code Path, Not a Prompt Instruction
nodes.rationale: No retrieval hits means the model is never called; no citations means the answer is treated as ungrounded. A prompt instruction is a request and a code path is a guarantee.
nodes.norm_label: abstention is a code path, not a prompt instruction

nodes.label: Minimal Hallucination Requirement
nodes.rationale: An internal knowledge assistant that invents a refund policy is worse than no assistant, because people act on it. Grounding solves this; protocols solve vendor agnosticism; everything else is consequence.

nodes.label: Vendor Agnosticism Requirement
nodes.rationale: Every model in this system will be replaced; the state of the art today will not be in eighteen months. Enforced by rule 1: business logic imports protocols and types only, never a provider — checkable with a grep.

nodes.label: Business Logic Never Imports a Provider
nodes.source_location: The two rules that hold it together
nodes.rationale: The single rule that makes vendor agnosticism real rather than aspirational. If a pipeline, route or CLI command ever imports providers/, the property is gone.
nodes.norm_label: business logic never imports a provider

nodes.label: integrations/ May Import the Core; the Core May Not
nodes.source_location: The two rules that hold it together
nodes.rationale: That one-way edge is what stops an outbound adapter — OSC's retriever exposed as a LangChain BaseRetriever — from becoming a dependency of the platform.
nodes.norm_label: integrations/ may import the core; the core may not

nodes.label: Protocols, Not Base Classes
nodes.rationale: Structural typing means a provider is compatible by virtue of its shape — no base class to inherit, no registration ceremony beyond one line. The practical consequence is that a test double is indistinguishable from a provider, which is what makes the API and CLI test suites meaningful rather than decorative.

nodes.label: One Datastore
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL holds chunk text, embeddings, the lexical index and document metadata. A chunk and its vector cannot drift apart, there is one backup, and hybrid retrieval is one round trip instead of two systems and a join in application code.

nodes.label: Frozen Prompts
nodes.rationale: Module constants with no interpolation so the prefix stays byte-identical. Anything dynamic breaks prefix caching and makes evaluation results unattributable — you would not know whether a score moved because retrieval changed or because the prompt did.

nodes.label: Instrumentation in Pipelines, Not Adapters
nodes.rationale: Every provider call is made from a pipeline, so wrapping the call sites covers all 37 providers without a single adapter importing the tracer — and a new provider is traced the day it is written.

nodes.label: Machine Output on stdout, Human Output on stderr
nodes.rationale: ./osc serve > run.log yields a clean parseable JSON log while the terminal still shows where the service is listening. Two audiences, two streams, neither compromised.
nodes.norm_label: machine output on stdout, human output on stderr

nodes.label: Operator Errors Are Messages; Bugs Are Tracebacks
nodes.rationale: AssistantError and its subclasses each carry an actionable message reported as one line. Anything else keeps its frames, because for a bug the frames are the point.
nodes.norm_label: operator errors are messages; bugs are tracebacks

nodes.label: workspace_id From Day One
nodes.rationale: The only speculative design in the codebase, defended on one ground: adding a partition key to a populated corpus is a data migration, and not adding it is a column. It began doing real work when two corpora came to share one database.

nodes.label: Frozen Dataclasses for Domain Types
nodes.rationale: These values are constructed internally and never parsed from untrusted input; validation belongs at the trust boundary — API schemas, settings, golden sets — not in the domain.

nodes.label: Where the Architecture Is Weakest
nodes.rationale: Stated openly because a knowledge base that only lists strengths is marketing. No authentication; citation strength differs by provider silently (nothing downstream can tell a verified citation from a parsed marker); the local answer model misreads figures (qwen3:8b rendered '500 to 2,500 EUR' as '50,000 to 2,500 EUR' while citing the correct passage); traces are process-local.

nodes.label: make verify
nodes.rationale: Runs every tier in a single pytest invocation — one summary line, one exit code, one list of failures. Three invocations would let a failure in the first scroll off the screen before the third finishes, the exact thing a canonical command prevents. -ra names every skip so a tier silently skipping for a missing database is visible rather than green. make verify asks whether the system is correct; make eval asks whether it is good.

nodes.label: Separate OSC_E2E_DSN and OSC_TEST_DSN
nodes.rationale: The E2E suite fixes its chunks table at the live embedding model's width and clears its workspace, so it needs a different database. With one variable between them only one tier could be pointed at the right place per run, and a single invocation would be impossible.

nodes.label: In-Process Protocol Test Doubles
nodes.source_location: What makes the fast tier meaningful
nodes.rationale: conftest.py holds in-process implementations of the protocols, not mocks. StubEmbeddingModel is a deterministic bag-of-words embedder hashing tokens into buckets so retrieval assertions are meaningful and identical on every machine with no model download; StubChatModel returns a scripted reply through the real marker-parsing citation path. They register through the ordinary registry — the same path a new provider takes — so 'the whole stack can be retargeted by configuration alone' is asserted by the suite rather than assumed.

nodes.label: Tests Never Assert Against the Production Corpus
nodes.rationale: A test asserting against docs/company/ content would start failing the day someone edited a document — a false alarm, and the fastest way to get a suite disabled. The line is content, not filenames: reading evaluation/suites/*.yaml or the configured corpus.root path is fine. The rule was violated and repaired: test_e2e.py ingested Path('docs') directly, which became two defects the moment that directory held real content — asserting against editable company documents and sweeping docs/engineering/ into the index.
nodes.norm_label: tests never assert against the production corpus

nodes.label: Tests Never Write Into the Working Directory
nodes.rationale: Trace and log persistence both default to on and write under .osc/; conftest redirects both per test via tmp_path, which also stops one test's records being visible to the next and making CLI assertions order-dependent. It calls shutdown_logging() on teardown because a leaked background listener writes a later test's records into a deleted tmp_path. test_cli.py purges every OSC_* variable and had re-applied only the trace dir, so every CLI test wrote into the developer's real .osc/logs.
nodes.norm_label: tests never write into the working directory

nodes.label: A Found Defect Gets a Regression Test in the Same Commit
nodes.rationale: The bold rows of the coverage table are that policy's output, and are the highest-value category of test in the suite — which is why the list is kept visible. A test asserts a behaviour, not an implementation: test_store_contract is parametrised over store implementations.
nodes.norm_label: a found defect gets a regression test in the same commit

nodes.label: Testing Known Gaps
nodes.rationale: Stated plainly because a testing document claiming completeness is not useful. No hosted provider has ever been called — including the Anthropic native-citation path, the only verified-citation implementation, asserted by reading SDK docs rather than by a test. No load test, no CI, the pgvector suite shares the application database, session memory is single-process only, and one E2E abstention assertion is deliberately tolerant because a live 8B model's abstention is not deterministic.

nodes.label: ADR 0003 — Hybrid Retrieval with RRF Fused in SQL
nodes.rationale: Retrieval bounds everything downstream, so the method choice is the highest-consequence decision in the pipeline. Alternatives rejected: vector-only (silently bad at pasted error strings and tags), keyword-only (useless for paraphrase), weighted score combination (needs normalising a cosine against an unbounded ts_rank plus a weight to re-derive whenever the embedding model changes), fusion in application code over two queries (two round trips, ranking logic in the hardest layer to test — also the specific reason LangChain's PGVector was not adopted), threshold after reranking, and cross-encoder on by default. Costs: rrf_k=60 is adopted on the paper's authority and never tuned here; two indexes to maintain; RRF discards score magnitude; min_score is nearly inert in hybrid mode; the lexical side is English-configured and nothing detects otherwise.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0003 — hybrid retrieval with rrf fused in sql

nodes.label: ADR 0008 — Deduplicate by Source, Not by Content
nodes.rationale: Keep source-keyed identity: the duplicate is a corpus problem, not a pipeline problem, and it is fixed by deleting a file. Detection is worth having; automatic collapse is not — it would silently discard a document an operator placed in the corpus and make behaviour depend on filesystem iteration order. Making document_id a hash of content would solve it and break incremental re-indexing, since identity would change on every edit and 'updated' could not be told from 'deleted and re-created'. Retrieval-time collapse treats the symptom and adds a text comparison to the hot path.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0008 — deduplicate by source, not by content

nodes.label: Byte-Identical Scenario Document Duplicate
nodes.rationale: Two .docx scenario files extract to byte-identical text (24,096 characters, hash 54314756e14a2f4f) while differing at the byte level, so nothing looks duplicated on disk. 34 of the index's 193 chunks (17.6%) are exact duplicates, and duplicate chunks compete for the same top_k=5 slots — a plausible contributor to four of six recall failures in faq-full.json retrieving a scenario chunk in place of the answering FAQ document. content_hash() answers 'has THIS document changed', keyed on document_id; nothing asks whether content matches a DIFFERENT document. Found by a knowledge-graph rebuild, which is not a control; the queued fix is a duplicates check in ./osc doctor via list_document_hashes().

nodes.label: ADR 0010 — The Corpus Root Is Configuration, Defined Once
nodes.rationale: ADR 0007 established the boundary well and the mechanism badly: the root was a literal in the Makefile, cli/diagnose.py and api/banner.py, kept equal by a rule for humans and a test covering only two of the three. A rule that survives only as long as everyone remembers it is a convention, not a boundary — and this one protects the corpus mistake that produces no error, warning or failing metric. Rejected: a third assertion (treats the symptom), a shared module constant (removes drift but keeps the root un-overridable per deployment, already wanted for the FAQ suite), and an exclusion list (fails open — a new internal directory is indexed by default; a directory boundary fails safe). Costs: make ingest no longer states what it ingests, and nothing stops a profile setting corpus.root: docs at runtime — the test catches it in CI.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0010 — the corpus root is configuration, defined once

nodes.label: ADR 0011 — The Schema Corpus Is the Authoritative Knowledge Source
nodes.rationale: Production ingest root becomes docs/company/schema/; the FAQ and scenario documents stay on disk unmodified and leave the index. Rejected: indexing both (keeps the baseline comparable but the two bodies overlap enough to be a real retrieval hazard), deleting the FAQ suite (deleting evaluation cases because they no longer match the corpus is the habit that makes a benchmark dishonest, and it is the only prose suite — the natural control), and migrating FAQ cases onto the schema corpus (would produce 86 abstention cases wearing the costume of a golden set). Costs: the quality baseline resets and is not comparable; the corpus got harder (abstention_accuracy 0.667, fact_match 0.782 vs 0.80/0.90); it exposed a chunker mismatch; the scenario documents are now unindexed and unscored.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0011 — the schema corpus is the authoritative knowledge source

nodes.label: The OSCP Schema Corpus
nodes.rationale: Eleven module persistence-schema documents — metafield inventories, metaobject field tables, Prisma models, sample payloads and ownership notes. Markdown tables and JSON rather than prose, which is why the chunker choice matters more here than it did on the FAQ.

nodes.label: Two Corpora, One Database, Partitioned by workspace_id
nodes.rationale: The partition key already existed on every table and is doing real work for the first time. The cost is that running the FAQ suite requires remembering the workspace; the suite file's header carries the command.
nodes.norm_label: two corpora, one database, partitioned by workspace_id

nodes.label: ADR 0012 — markdown Becomes the Default Chunker, on a Measurement
nodes.rationale: All four strategies were run against the schema suite with everything else held constant, each after a full --reindex because chunk ids derive from boundaries and an ordinary sync would report 'skipped' and silently measure the old index under the new label. markdown wins on every metric (recall@5 0.982 vs recursive's 0.909; 80 chunks vs 52), with precision@5 0.200 the structural maximum. Rejected: raising chunk_size on recursive (treats a structural problem as a sizing problem — the boundary is in the wrong place, not merely too close), fixed (rejected on the numbers, but beating recursive suggests recursive's separator ladder actively mis-fires on table syntax), and preprocessing tables into sentences (parsers extract and never rewrite, because chunk text is quoted back as citation evidence and invented text would make that evidence a forgery). Costs: every chunk id changed, the index grew 54%, the median chunk shrank 826→278 characters, and top_k was deliberately not re-tuned because two variables moving at once is how a measurement stops meaning anything. The result is corpus-specific and must not be generalised.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0012 — markdown becomes the default chunker, on a measurement

nodes.label: ADR 0013 — Conversational Memory Is Ephemeral, Process-Local and Bounded
nodes.rationale: Answerer.answer/stream and QueryRewriter already took history; what was missing was somewhere for the conversation to live between turns — which made this a question about storage, and storage is where a conversational feature usually acquires a database table it did not need. Rejected: a conversations table (write load on the primary datastore for a feature needing no durability, plus a second place user text is retained with its own retention story), Redis (a dependency, a deployment component and a failure mode for a single-process deployment), client-held history as the default (puts the security boundary in the client — a caller replaying a transcript can replay any transcript, and with no authentication there is nothing to check it against), and summarising older turns (a model call per turn on the critical path to compress context bounded at ten exchanges).
nodes.norm_label: adr 0013 — conversational memory is ephemeral, process-local and bounded

nodes.label: InMemorySessionStore
nodes.rationale: An OrderedDict with LRU eviction, per-session message trimming and idle expiry swept on access. Bounded three ways because an unbounded conversation store fails in three unrelated ways: max_messages 20 (a long conversation growing the prompt until generation truncates), max_sessions 1000 (a client that never closes), idle_ttl_seconds 3600 (a browser tab closed without a DELETE). Trimming is from the front because a follow-up refers to what was just said. Session ids are secrets.token_hex(16) — unguessability is load-bearing because no endpoint is authenticated, so the session id is the only thing between two users' conversations. Not thread-safe, and does not need to be: awaited from one event loop with no await between reading and mutating.

nodes.label: Conversation
nodes.rationale: Binds a store to an Answerer — read history, answer against it, record the exchange. It exists so the three call sites that need it (buffered route, streaming route, evaluation harness) share one definition of what a turn is. An abstention is recorded as a turn, because dropping it would leave a follow-up like 'why not?' with nothing to resolve against. A stream that fails partway records nothing: the turn is recorded on AnswerComplete alone, because that event is authoritative and concatenated deltas would sometimes write history the user never saw.

nodes.label: History Reaches Generation but Not Retrieval
nodes.rationale: Retrieval sees history only through QueryRewriter. With rewrite_queries: false a follow-up is generated with full context and retrieved for as if it were standalone. follow_up_lift measured exactly 0.0 on the default profile, which is what made the gap a number rather than a suspicion.
nodes.norm_label: history reaches generation but not retrieval

nodes.label: Memory Does Not Survive a Restart
nodes.rationale: An expired or unknown session is a 404 naming the three ordinary causes — closed, idled out, service restarted — and the client's correct response to all three is to open a new session. Behind more than one replica a client's next turn may reach a process that never heard of its session, so sticky sessions or a shared store is a prerequisite for horizontal scaling.
nodes.norm_label: memory does not survive a restart

nodes.label: ADR 0014 — Regression Tolerances Are Derived, Not Typed
nodes.rationale: Phase 4's gate was --fail-under recall@5=0.90, an arbitrary number: 0.90 was a round number below the 0.932 baseline and corresponds to no property of the measurement. It did not track the suite size, could not distinguish noise from regression (retrieval is deterministic, generation is sampled — one flat threshold is either too tight or too loose, so generation was simply not gated), and checked each metric alone. Rejected: more flags (scales the problem), a flat generation threshold (too wide to catch a real regression), bootstrap confidence intervals (more correct at small n and p→1, deferred on cost/benefit with a MINIMUM_TOLERANCE floor handling the known weakness), and a held-out gating set (methodologically correct, needs roughly twice the curated cases).
nodes.norm_label: adr 0014 — regression tolerances are derived, not typed

nodes.label: Derived Per-Metric Tolerances
nodes.rationale: Retrieval gets 1/n — one case — because it is deterministic for a fixed index, so the tolerance is a materiality threshold and 'more than one case was lost' is the only unit a person reading a red build can act on. Generation, citations and abstention get 2×√(p(1−p)/n), two standard errors of a binomial proportion: a drop inside it is indistinguishable from re-running the same commit. Latency is 25% relative and warning-only because it is heavy-tailed and machine-dependent. Counts are not gated because they describe the run's size, not its quality. n is the cases that actually contributed to that metric. Consequence: a small suite has wide tolerances visibly (abstention_accuracy over six cases tolerates ~0.385), and groundedness at p=1.0 falls to the 0.005 floor so any real drop fails — intended, because a fabricated citation is not a quality trade-off to be balanced.

nodes.label: Trade-off Guards
nodes.rationale: Check pairs rather than metrics, each naming a real way to game the suite: precision@k bought with recall@k (return fewer results), abstention_accuracy bought with citation_coverage (abstain more often), latency_p50 bought with recall@k (retrieve fewer candidates). When both halves move beyond their own tolerances in opposite directions the gate blocks regardless of how good the improving half looks alone — so the gate can block a change whose headline metric improved, which is the point.

nodes.label: The Gate Explains Itself
nodes.rationale: Every finding carries previous value, current value, delta, the tolerance used, the sentence saying where that tolerance came from, severity, the cases that changed from passing to failing, and the categories they span. A gate that prints 'recall@5 failed' is a gate someone overrides.

nodes.author: Brown, Cai & DasGupta
nodes.norm_label: brown, cai & dasgupta, interval estimation for a binomial proportion (2001)

nodes.label: ADR Process and Rules
nodes.rationale: An ADR records why a decision was made, what else was considered and what it costs — the code says what was decided, only this says why. It prevents re-litigating settled questions and reversing a decision without knowing its cost. Rules: ADRs are append-only (superseding means writing a new record, because why a past decision was right at the time tells you which assumption changed); a record is written when the decision is made, not reconstructed later; consequences include the costs, because a record listing only benefits is advocacy and nobody trusts it twice.

nodes.label: Committed Baselines Directory
nodes.rationale: evaluation/results/ is gitignored and holds every run; this directory holds the few that are trusted, committed so a regression is a diff rather than a memory. Named <suite>-<variant>.json, which _default_baseline() in cli/evaluate.py computes so a suite is gated against its own baseline automatically. Retrieval-only and full runs have separate baselines on purpose: comparing one against the other would silently diff the intersection of two different measurements. Re-baselining to make a red build green without a recorded reason is the one thing this directory exists to make visible.

nodes.label: The FAQ Baselines Are Historical
nodes.rationale: faq-*.json were full-default.json and retrieval-default.json through Phase 5. Kept, not deleted: they are the measurement record behind ADR 0003 and ADR 0008, and deleting evidence because the system moved on is how a benchmark becomes a story. Their numbers are not comparable to the schema suite's, and PROJECT_STATUS.md reports both labelled.

nodes.label: Schema Golden Set Suite
nodes.rationale: Four rules, each existing because breaking it produces a number that looks fine and measures nothing: questions phrased the way an engineer would ask them rather than copied from headings; expected_facts short, distinctive and load-bearing (adt, cartTransformId, registractionForm, IDEMPOTENCY_WINDOW_MS — strings that appear nowhere else and cannot be produced by a plausible-sounding guess); facts drawn from the document body not the question, since a fact the question already contains is scored on echo and an extractive model passes it without retrieving; and abstention cases naming things the corpus genuinely does not cover, which these persistence schemas make easy because they deliberately push architecture, routes, events and UX into a README that is not in the corpus.

nodes.label: Conversational Golden Set Suite
nodes.rationale: 18 sessions over docs/company/schema. Each case runs its turns in order through the real Conversation, the real SessionStore and the real pipelines. References are written the way people actually type them; turn one of every case is standalone, because a case opening with a reference would measure nothing but the abstention policy.

nodes.label: Cold Control Run and follow_up_lift
nodes.source_location: What makes a multi-turn case worth having
nodes.rationale: The interesting question is never 'did the follow-up get answered' but 'could it have been answered without the conversation'. A follow-up that retrieves the right document by keyword luck proves nothing about memory, so every requires_context turn is re-run in a fresh empty session as a control; follow_up_lift is the difference and is the only honest measure of what conversational memory contributes. A lift near zero means the follow-ups are not actually context dependent — a defect in the golden set, not the system, and one that is invisible otherwise.

nodes.label: Conversational Turn Flags
nodes.rationale: requires_context marks a turn not answerable standalone (a pronoun, ellipsis or bare ordinal) and enrolls it in the control run. context_switch marks a standalone turn about a different document, measuring the opposite failure — history dragging retrieval back to the previous topic — where the cold control is the benchmark to match rather than beat. must_abstain inside a conversation is the harder case: the model has relevant-looking history in front of it and must still decline.

nodes.label: FAQ Golden Set Suite (preserved, not production)
nodes.rationale: 86 curated cases and a committed baseline representing real measurement work. Kept unmodified because deleting evaluation cases that no longer match the current corpus is exactly the habit that makes a benchmark dishonest, and because it remains the only suite over prose documents — the control when a chunker or retrieval change is suspected of being specific to the schema corpus's tables and JSON. Run under OSC_WORKSPACE_ID=faq, which is what keeps the two corpora from sharing an index.
nodes.norm_label: faq golden set suite (preserved, not production)

nodes.label: Bundled Chat UI
nodes.rationale: Deliberately one self-contained file with no build step and no framework. It talks to the same public API as any other client — POST /api/chat, then read the SSE stream — and nothing here is imported by the backend, so the whole UI can be replaced by swapping this file, which is the expected path.

nodes.label: The complete Event Is Authoritative
nodes.rationale: When the complete event reports an abstention the client must discard the text it already rendered, because the assistant declined to answer. The handler replaces whatever streamed, re-renders sources as empty on abstention, and this is one of two rules the file asks a rewrite to preserve.

nodes.label: Client Session Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: One server-held session per page load: the client keeps an id, not a transcript, so a reload starts a clean conversation and closing the tab releases the memory. sendBeacon cannot issue a DELETE, so the pagehide handler uses fetch with keepalive — an ordinary fetch is cancelled when the page goes away and the session would wait out its idle TTL instead. The submit handler awaits sessionReady before the first turn so question one is part of the conversation rather than an orphan the second turn cannot refer to, and degrades to single-turn behaviour when the session could not be opened. The API takes session_id or history, never both.

nodes.label: SSE Frame Parsing Loop
nodes.rationale: Frames are separated by a blank line and a partial frame stays buffered across reads. Handles sources, delta, citation, complete and error events; citations accumulate into a Set of chunk ids that re-renders the source list with cited boxes highlighted.
